chunks: And among what he narrated—also from Faḍālah, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Wipe the head over its front and its back.”

So both are to be understood as having been stated under taqiyyah, because they conflict with the Qur'an according to what we have mentioned, and they repulse the reports according to what we have established. Contradiction in their speech is not permissible, nor can there be heard from them that which conflicts with the Qur'an; and this confirms what we have mentioned.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: Dissimulation practiced under circumstances requiring precaution
key_terms.الرَّأْسَ: The head, the area to be wiped in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارَ: The transmitted reports or hadith narrations
key_terms.الْقُرْآنَ: The Qur'an, the primary revealed criterion
key_terms.مُؤَخَّرِهِ: Its back part, referring to the back of the head
key_terms.مُقَدَّمِهِ: Its front part, referring to the front of the head

ai.seo_question: Why is the narration about wiping the front and back of the head in wudu interpreted as taqiyyah?
ai.summary: This passage concerns the ruling of wiping the head in wudu (ablution) and explains that a report ظاهرًا indicating wiping both the front and back of the head is interpreted in light of taqiyyah. The text stresses that the teachings of the Imams عليهم السلام do not contradict the Qur'an, and that reports must be understood in harmony with the Qur'an and other established narrations.
